title: Counting pulses in Ladder: a CTU counts the edges itself
summary: Place a CTU in a rung so that CountReached turns on at the third rising edge of a pulse input and Reset clears the count.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence with one 10 ms task; they do not establish the counting accuracy of a real input, wiring, hardware timing, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Place a counter block in a rung and set its preset and its reset.
Explain that a counter adds one on the rising edge of its input, not on every scan in which the input is high.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/EdgeCounterLd.ld.json one rung copies PulseInput to CountReached. Replace the copy with a CTU of preset 3 between the contact and the coil, and wire Reset to its R input, so that CountReached turns on at the third pulse and Reset clears it.
stages.checkpoint: The counter sits between PulseInput and the coil of CountReached.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: PulseInput goes high at {{t:10}}, {{t:30}} and {{t:50}} ms, one scan each time. Reset is pressed at {{t:70}} ms. Predict CountReached at {{t:30}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:70}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:EdgeCounterLd.CountReached=false@30|OFF}} at {{t:30}} ms, only two pulses so far; {{v:EdgeCounterLd.CountReached=true@50|ON}} at {{t:50}} ms, on the third; {{v:EdgeCounterLd.CountReached=false@70|OFF}} at {{t:70}} ms, after Reset.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press Check: The starter copies the pulse to the coil: CountReached is ON at {{t:10}} ms, on the first pulse, instead of after the third; place a CTU with PV 3, Reset on its R input, between PulseInput and CountReached. In the Ladder editor drag a CTU block between the contact and the coil, name its instance Count, and set PV to 3 and R to Reset.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named EdgeCounterLd and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:30}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:70}} ms: CountReached rises once, at the third pulse, and falls once, when Reset clears the count.
stages.checkpoint: CountReached rises once at {{t:50}} ms and falls once at {{t:70}} ms.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Replace the plain contact in front of the CTU with a positive-transition contact and run again. Why does the result not change?
stages.checkpoint: The CTU already counts only the change from FALSE to TRUE of its input, so a pulse counts once however many scans it stays high; the edge contact only repeats what the block does. A pulse that rises while Reset is held is lost.

hints.text: A coil only shows the power that reaches it. Which block remembers how many times the power has risen?
Place a CTU between PulseInput and CountReached, name the instance Count, and set PV to 3 and R to Reset. The coil takes the output of the block.

faultCases: The starter copies the pulse to the coil: CountReached is ON at {{t:10}} ms, on the first pulse, instead of after the third; place a CTU with PV 3, Reset on its R input, between PulseInput and CountReached.
